title: Velocity-Time Graph (0–10s Trapezoid Motion)
subject: Physics
description: A velocity-time graph rising linearly from (0s, 0 m/s) to (4s, 20 m/s), staying flat until (8s, 20 m/s), then dropping linearly to (10s, 0 m/s).

structured_extraction.key_concept: Area under a velocity-time curve equals total displacement; slope equals acceleration.
socratic_checkpoints: Notice the graph has three simple geometric regions between the line and the time axis. What two shapes do you see?
How do you compute the area of the first triangle from t=0s to t=4s (base = 4s, height = 20 m/s)?
Now add the middle rectangle (4s to 8s) and the final triangle (8s to 10s) — what sum do you get for total displacement?

title: Free-Body Diagram: 4 kg Block on 30° Frictionless Ramp
subject: Physics
description: A 4 kg block resting on a smooth 30-degree inclined plane showing weight vector mg downward and normal force N perpendicular to the ramp.

structured_extraction.key_concept: Resolve gravitational weight mg into parallel (mg sin theta) and perpendicular (mg cos theta) components.
socratic_checkpoints: Weight mg acts straight down, not along the ramp. Which trig function (sin or cos) gives the component pulling the block parallel down a 30-degree slope?
Using sin(30°) = 0.5 and g = 9.8 m/s², what is the parallel force mg·sin(30°) for a 4 kg block?
Divide that net force by the 4 kg mass (or use a = g·sin(30°)) — does the mass even affect the acceleration on a frictionless ramp?

title: Enzyme Reaction Rate vs. Temperature Curve
subject: Biology
description: An asymmetric reaction rate curve peaking at 37 C and plunging sharply toward zero between 42 C and 55 C.

structured_extraction.key_concept: Kinetic energy increases collisions up to 37 C; higher heat breaks bonds and denatures the active site.
socratic_checkpoints: Look at the shape on the left vs. right of the 37 C peak. Why do you think the right side drops off so much steeper than the left side rises?
What happens to the weak hydrogen bonds holding an enzyme's 3D active site together when thermal energy gets too high?
If the active site permanently changes shape, why can the substrate no longer form an enzyme-substrate complex?
structured_extraction.target_numeric_answer: Denaturation of the active site above 37 C
